summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, bladder and prostate cancer s/p ileal conduit, and chronic anemia presented after a fall due to lightheadedness and weakness. He had a recent episode of stoma bleeding sutured in the ED and was found to have acute on chronic blood loss anemia, requiring one unit of packed red blood cells. His fall was attributed to alcohol intoxication (ETOH 96), possible orthostasis, and anemia. He exhibited transient left facial droop and weakness, prompting neurology consultation and recommendation for non-urgent MRI to rule out stroke. Toxic encephalopathy was suspected due to alcohol use, though he remained alert. Urinalysis revealed pyuria with a positive culture for Klebsiella pneumoniae, though antibiotics were withheld due to absence of systemic infection. Abdominal ultrasound showed patent hepatic vasculature with reversed flow in the left portal vein, no ascites, and mild left hydronephrosis. The patient became agitated, refused further testing, and left against medical advice after stabilization. He was advised to follow up with neurology, urology, and hepatology.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Alcoholic cirrhosis of liver without ascites
Hemorrhage of continent stoma of urinary tract
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
Iron deficiency anemia secondary to blood loss (chronic)
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of bladder
Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
